newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore share index ends up in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore share index ends up in quiet trade.

text.p: Singapore's key share index finished marginally higher in quiet trading on Tuesday with two rumoured takeover target stocks dominating volume and gains.
Brokers said that but for the two stocks -- Transmarco and Metro Holdings -- the volume would have been still thinner.
The key Straits Times Industrials Index ended 11.42 points up at 2,171.45 on a volume of only 83.90 million shares. Decliners led rises by 219 to 87.

Retailer Metro Holdings rose Singapore S$0.20 to S$5.55 on volume of 5.34 million shares as punters continued to pin hopes on a takeover of the company. Metro said on Friday it has no idea why its shares started rising.

Trading and telecommunication company Transmarco rose S$0.40 to S$10.30 after touching a morning high of S$11.50 on news that Indonesian tycoon Putera Sampoerna had upped his bid for the company to S$9.45 per share after buying a 30 percent stake from major shareholder Sukamto Sia.

Its volume of 10.28 million shares included the block of 8.2 million shares sold by Sukamto to Sampoerna's investment company Miel Investment at S$9.45. SIA Foreign led gainers, rising S$0.30 to S$14.80.
